![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14145046/assets/d457bfe2ac8b0a86da15e2c34704ae5011a58ad8c148905aa1df12a674544f6c.png)

What are the $y$-intercepts of the parabola shown above?
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(-9,5)$ and passes through the point $(7,1).$

The general standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola with vertex at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h),
$$

and substituting $(h,k)=(-9,5)$ into the above gives

$$
(y-5)^{2}=4p(x+9).
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(7,1),$ we substitute $x=7$ and $y=1$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(1-5)^{2} & =4p(7+9) \\ 16 & =4p(16) \\ p & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-5)^{2} & =(x+9).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$ So, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-5)^{2} & =(0+9) \\ (y-5)^{2} & =9 \\ y-5 & =\pm 3 \\ y & =5\pm 3 \\ y & =2,8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $y$-intercepts are $2$
and $8.$
